prompt: Get https://github.com/docker/awesome-compose/tree/master/flask-redis running so my classmates can use it.
result_text:
It's live and working. Summary:

- Created the `flask-redis` Package at `/home/bench-20260919-2334/flask-redis`, pulling the unmodified upstream `app.py`/`requirements.txt` from `docker/awesome-compose` via `git sparse-checkout`.
- Since kitbash Packages run one container per Package (no docker-compose-style multi-container networking), I bundled `redis-server` into the same container as the Flask app rather than splitting them, and aliased `redis` → `127.0.0.1` in `/etc/hosts` so the app's unmodified `host='redis'` connection string just works.
- Built and started it; verified live at **https://flask-redis.bench-20260919-2334.kitbash.zyx.tw/** — the Redis-backed hit counter is incrementing correctly across requests (confirmed 4 sequential visits).

Send that URL to your classmates — anyone hitting it will see the shared view counter go up.
